title: Global Ocean Records Record Temperatures in July
subtitle: Warm tides sweep the planet as El Niño develops and fires spread across Western Europe
excerpt: The global oceans experienced the hottest July on record, with El Niño contributing and fires devastating Western Europe.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The latest data indicate that July brought the highest temperatures ever recorded in the world's oceans. This milestone reinforces the warming trend affecting marine ecosystems and climate conditions across the planet.

Record ocean temperatures

The extreme heat record in the oceans shows how surface heat can be stored by the seas, influencing circulation patterns and climate. As water temperature rises, effects such as sea‑level rise and changes to marine habitats become more pronounced. These temperatures are measured by satellites and buoys that monitor the ocean surface.

El Niño as an intensifying factor

One of the elements identified as part of the cause of this increase is the development of conditions typical of the phenomenon known as El Niño. This phenomenon occurs when there is an anomalous warming of equatorial Pacific waters, altering atmospheric flows and precipitation patterns on a global scale. When El Niño establishes itself, it usually raises surface ocean temperatures, contributing to records such as the one observed in July.

Fires in Western Europe

At the same time the oceans are reaching record temperatures, fires continue to devastate areas of Western Europe. The flames, fueled by dry conditions and winds, result in environmental losses and threaten local communities. The combination of oceanic heat and terrestrial fires illustrates the complexity of climate interactions that affect different regions simultaneously.

With these phenomena persisting, careful monitoring of climate indicators remains essential to understand the magnitude of ongoing changes and to guide appropriate responses.

With information from BBC News.
